findings.title: save_pack is the one Vault write that is not serialised: a double click on '저장 (commit)' makes the second request fail with 500 on the shared temp file; other interleavings answer 200 for a text that was not committed or leave a loader-rejected pack.yaml on disk
findings.story: Every write of HubService is wrapped in @_serialised ('a double click or two tabs must not race each other') — except save_pack. Both requests write the same packs/<name>/pack.yaml.tmp, then move it. The first move takes the file; the second finds nothing and dies with FileNotFoundError → 500 'filesystem error', although the pack was saved. TLC found two more outcomes of the same missing lock: a request answers 200 after loading the *other* request's text (P5), and two loader-rejected saves leave a rejected pack.yaml behind because one restores the other's bad text as its 'backup' (P4). Only the double-click trace (P7) was replayed against the code; the P4 and P5 traces are model results with the same root cause and the same fix.

findings.title: save_pack is not all-or-nothing: when the commit is refused (pre-commit device, git error) the new pack.yaml stays written and staged although the request answered 500
findings.story: ADR-0009: every Hub write ends in exactly one commit and leaves the Vault untouched or fully committed. The other writes get this from _mutation(); save_pack wrote pack.yaml, and when _commit failed the file (and copied sidecars) stayed on disk and in the git index. The user sees '저장 실패' while the pack is in fact active on the next load.

fix.summary: On any failure after the first write (loader rejection or refused commit) _undo_pack_write restores pack.yaml to its previous bytes (or removes it), removes the sidecar files this request copied and the directories it created, restores .gitignore and unstages packs/<name>.
